run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: In app-265-prod-logs the whole 24h window holds only 7 documents (all shown), so this is a very thin sample rather than a fleet survey. Three are ERROR and all three carry cluster=production-us-east-1: checkout-service logged a failed POST /api/checkout due to a 30s payment-provider response timeout named (stripe-us) at 08:06:17Z, payment-service logged an upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms at 09:06:17Z, and checkout-service then logged a circuit breaker open for payment-service with failure rate 41% at 09:36:17Z. The four INFO documents come from the other two clusters (production-eu-west-2, production-ap-southeast-1) and report healthy checkout/payment conditions, including 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms'. The Kubernetes cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2, namespace otel-demo) is healthy in every check I made: all 25 deployments 1/1 available, pods Running, payment and checkout pods logging only successful charges/orders up to 10:05:51Z, and the flagd fault flags all defaulting to off. So the observed failure is confined to the production-us-east-1 payment path and traces to the external provider stripe-us; I could not verify it further because Prometheus and Jaeger queries all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and I have no Kubernetes access to production-us-east-1.

claims.text: The index app-265-prod-logs mapped fields cluster, level, message, service and timestamp, and the pattern app-265-prod-logs* matched exactly one open green index with docs.count 7.

Over the full authorized window the index returned exactly 7 documents: 3 at level ERROR and 4 at level INFO; by cluster field 3 documents are production-us-east-1, 2 production-eu-west-2 and 2 production-ap-southeast-1; the documents are timestamped 08:06:17Z, 09:06:17Z and 09:36:17Z.
checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged at 2026-11-22T08:06:17Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.
payment-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged at 2026-11-22T09:06:17Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged at 2026-11-22T09:36:17Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'.

The non-us documents report healthy conditions for the same services: production-eu-west-2 checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' at 08:06:17Z and production-eu-west-2 payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' at 09:36:17Z; production-ap-southeast-1 checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' at 08:06:17Z and production-ap-southeast-1 payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 09:36:17Z. This argues against a fleet-wide provider outage.

In the cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2), all 25 deployments including checkout and payment report ready=1 and available=1 of replicas=1 with no unavailable replicas, and no pod is in a non-Running phase.

The payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d in namespace otel-demo logged only successful charges ('Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.') between 09:25:02Z and 10:05:51Z, with no error lines in the 100 newest of 369 lines read.

The checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n in namespace otel-demo logged successful order flow at 10:04:16Z and 10:05:51Z including 'payment went through (transaction_id: 59347df9-4c19-4704-91b1-3012850a7f95)' and '(transaction_id: 818e6db9-27db-4371-aef0-04ede83e9dd8)'.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo holds demo.flagd.json in which every fault flag (including paymentFailure 'Fail payment service charge requests n%' and paymentUnreachable 'Payment service is unavailable') has defaultVariant 'off' and no switch is set to an on value.

Across all namespaces the only events inside the window are two Warning events with reason FailedToCreateEndpoint: Endpoints 'orca' in app-95 at 09:21:00Z ('endpoints "orca" already exists') and Endpoints 'signup-service' in app-162 at 09:32:52Z ('endpoints "signup-service" already exists').

The prometheus-readonly-proxy pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (6 restarts) has a previous nginx container that died logging 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"' at 08:04:42Z, and its current container produced no log lines in the window.

The prometheus-server container is running and logging continuously (231 'Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars' warnings up to 10:06:21Z) and jaeger logged a startup sequence at 08:04:21Z configuring metrics reader ServerURL http://prometheus:9090 with grpc 'connection refused' to localhost:4317; both pods are Running and ready.

The originating fault is the external payment provider stripe-us failing to answer /v1/charges within 30s for production-us-east-1: payment-service reports the upstream timeout and checkout-service then fails POST /api/checkout and opens its circuit breaker for payment-service at 41% failure rate.

An alternative unverified cause is the network/DNS path from production-us-east-1 to stripe-us rather than the provider itself: the logs prove a timeout awaiting the upstream, not which side was slow.

A fault-injection flag (paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable in a flagd configuration) in production-us-east-1 could produce exactly this payment/checkout failure pattern; that cluster's flagd ConfigMap is not readable from my access, so this remains untested rather than excluded.

Rejected for the cluster I can read: a Kubernetes workload fault in production-eu-west-2 otel-demo was not the cause, since all 25 deployments were 1/1 available and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged only completed transactions/orders through 10:05:51Z.
Rejected for production-eu-west-2: an enabled fault-injection flag did not cause any restart or failure there, because demo.flagd.json has every flag at defaultVariant 'off'.

No document in app-265-prod-logs during the window names a service other than checkout-service and payment-service, and the only ERROR documents are the three production-us-east-1 ones; the index is therefore too sparse to show whether other fleet services were impacted.

gaps: Prometheus queries (get_all_labels, get_label_values, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target) and Jaeger queries (traces_search, traces_list_services) all failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE during this run, so there is no error-rate, latency or trace evidence to quantify the failure rate, establish when it began, or confirm whether it persists after 09:36:17Z.

Kubernetes access is limited to cluster production-eu-west-2, so the affected production-us-east-1 payment-service and checkout-service pods, their events, container statuses and ConfigMaps (including any flagd fault flags) could not be inspected; all us-east-1 findings rest on log documents only.

app-265-prod-logs contains only 7 documents in the whole 24h authorized window, so absence of errors for other fleet clusters or services is not evidence that they were healthy; only the four INFO documents from production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 were observed.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so no deployment, configuration or feature-flag change timeline is available for the incident window.
It is unknown whether the stripe-us timeouts are provider-side or caused by network egress/DNS from production-us-east-1; no connectivity or provider-status evidence was available.

The cause of the prometheus-readonly-proxy container crash at 08:04:42Z (host not found in upstream 'prometheus:9090') and whether it explains the SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE metric/trace errors could not be verified; no client-side evidence of the gateway path was readable.
next_steps: Check the stripe-us provider status/incident feed and production-us-east-1 egress/DNS to the provider for the 08:00-10:06Z period.

Once Prometheus is reachable, measure error rate and p95/p99 latency for payment-service and checkout-service (and the circuit-breaker open ratio) restricted to cluster production-us-east-1, comparing against production-eu-west-2 as baseline.
Inspect production-us-east-1 Kubernetes objects: payment/checkout pod status, restart counts, events, and the flagd ConfigMap values for paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable.
Confirm whether checkout-service's circuit breaker to payment-service is still open and whether orders are failing after 09:36:17Z.
Repair or confirm the health of the metrics path (prometheus-readonly-proxy restarts, prometheus:9090 DNS resolution) so alerting and dashboards are trustworthy during this incident.
